<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Siddhahema&quot; is a Sanskrit grammar text. The full title of the text is &quot; Siddhahemaśabdānuśāsana&quot;, which can be translated as &quot;The Established Explanation of the Meanings of Words According to Hemacandra.&quot; The text is a commentary on the &quot; Aṣṭādhyāyī &quot;, a foundational work of Sanskrit grammar written by Panini in the 4th century BCE. Hemacandra's commentary is written in verse, and it provides a detailed analysis of Panini's grammar, along with examples and explanations of its rules and concepts.<br><br>&quot;Siddhahema&quot; is considered to be one of the most important commentaries on the &quot;Aṣṭādhyāyī&quot;, and it has been widely studied and commented on by scholars of Sanskrit grammar. The text is noted for its clarity and precision, and for its ability to make the complex and sometimes arcane rules of Panini's grammar accessible to a wider audience.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot; Siddhahemaśabdānuśāsana &quot; is a Sanskrit grammar text written by Hemacandra, a renowned scholar and poet of 12th century India. It is a commentary on the &quot;Aṣṭādhyāyī&quot;, a foundational work of Sanskrit grammar written by Panini in the 4th century BCE. The &quot;Siddhahema&quot; is organized into eight chapters, or Prakaraṇas, which cover the following topics:<br>1. Paribhāṣā -Prakaraṇa: This chapter provides an introduction to the text and defines key terms and concepts used throughout the commentary.<br>2. Prakriyā-Prakaraṇa: This chapter discusses the various methods used in the &quot;Aṣṭādhyāyī&quot; for forming words and sentences, including the use of affixes, roots, and sandhi (the merging of sounds at the junction of two words).<br>3. Linga-Prakaraṇa: This chapter explains the concept of grammatical gender in Sanskrit, including the various categories of gender and the rules for determining gender.<br>4. Vibhakti-Prakaraṇa: This chapter discusses the cases (vibhaktis) used in Sanskrit grammar, including their forms, meanings, and usage.<br>5. Samāsa-Prakaraṇa: This chapter explains the rules for forming compound words in Sanskrit, including the different types of compounds and their meanings.<br>6. Kāraka-Prakaraṇa: This chapter discusses the concept of karakas (case roles) in Sanskrit grammar, including their types, meanings, and usage.<br>7. Avyaya-Prakaraṇa: This chapter explains the various types of avyayas (indeclinables) used in Sanskrit grammar, including adverbs, particles, and interjections.<br>8. Paribhāṣā -Prakaraṇa: This final chapter provides a summary of the main points covered in the commentary and concludes with a benediction.</div></div></div>

The &quot;Siddhahema&quot; is widely regarded as one of the most important commentaries on the &quot;Aṣṭādhyāyī&quot;, and it is noted for its clarity, precision, and systematic approach to explaining the complex rules and concepts of Sanskrit grammar. Some of the unique features of the &quot;Siddhahema&quot;:<br><br>1. Comprehensive coverage: The &quot;Siddhahema&quot; covers all aspects of Sanskrit grammar as presented in the &quot;Aṣṭādhyāyī&quot;, including word formation, gender, cases, compound words, case roles, and indeclinable.<br>2. Clear explanations: Hemacandra's commentary is written in clear and simple language, making the complex rules and concepts of Panini's grammar accessible to a wider audience. He provides numerous examples and illustrations to help readers understand the grammar rules.<br>3. Systematic organization: The &quot;Siddhahema&quot; is organized into eight chapters, each of which covers a specific aspect of Sanskrit grammar. This systematic approach makes it easy for readers to navigate and understand the complex grammar rules.<br>4. Critical evaluation: Hemacandra's commentary includes a critical evaluation of Panini's grammar, pointing out errors and inconsistencies in the original text and offering alternative explanations and interpretations.<br>5. Influence on Sanskrit grammar: The &quot;Siddhahema&quot; has had a profound influence on the study and teaching of Sanskrit grammar. Its clear explanations and systematic approach have made it a valuable resource for scholars and students of Sanskrit linguistics for centuries.</div></div></div>
